title: Control plane private endpoint authorization and subnet stitching for safe upgrades
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: private deployments require tighter control over which VPCs and subnets can reach the private control plane. Existing private-installer allowed broad endpoint access and relied on coarse subnet placement for upgrades which made safe rollouts cumbersome. This PR introduces two complementary changes: (1) explicit private endpoint authorization via security-tagged security groups and endpoint policies so cross-account and cross-VPC peering can be granted programmatically; (2) deterministic subnet stitching and a maintenance-subnet handoff mechanism that lets the installer move controlplane workloads between subnets during upgrades with a safe drain/rollback path.

Summary of changes: - Terraform: add module terraform/modules/controlplane/endpoint_authorization that creates aws_vpc_endpoint_service_permissions, aws_vpc_endpoint_policy (when using Privatelink), and helper IAM role for cross-account acceptance. Introduces a security tag scheme (redwood:cp-access=[env,owner]) used to label SGs. - Terraform: add terraform/modules/controlplane/subnet_stitching which provisions maintenance subnets and a lifecycle policy that annotates previous subnets for rollback window. - Helm chart: update charts/private-installer/templates/controlplane-deployment.yaml to support an init container that verifies endpoint reachability and marks readiness only after the stitching handoff completes. - Installer CLI: add commands bin/rwpi subnet stitch --from <subnet-id> --to <subnet-id> and bin/rwpi endpoint authorize --peer-account <acct-id> which call the underlying Terraform controller and wait for acceptance. - Tests: integration harness updates under test/e2e/privatelink and new unit tests for the Terraform plan diffs. - Docs: docs/private-installer/endpoint-auth.md and docs/private-installer/subnet-stitching.md with operation runbooks and rollback steps.

Checklist (included in description as a single string): - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit tested - [x] Helm chart changes with health-probe integration - [x] Installer CLI commands with feature flags behind "stitching" opt-in - [x] E2E test added to nightly suite - [x] Security review: SG tagging and IAM bounded to required actions - [x] Internal docs and runbooks added

Why this is safe: endpoint authorization is opt-in and gated behind a new Boolean var controlplane.endpoint_authorization_enabled (default: false). Subnet stitching requires explicit staging labels on subnets and the installer will refuse to stitch unless both sides have matching stitch:allow tags. The Terraform plan includes a TTL annotation for rollback (stitching.rollback_ttl_days) so stale handoffs are automatically considered unsafe and must be explicitly overridden.

Migration notes: operators upgrading from older installer versions will see a no-op unless they enable endpoint_authorization_enabled and provision maintenance subnets. The included docs have a step-by-step guide for enabling the feature in production clusters, including sample Linear/Jira tracking templates for cross-account acceptance flows.

Commits summary: see commits field for high-level commits.

Related: builds on prior work for maintenance subnets (ENG-3621) and cross-account peering automation (SUP-872).

release_notes: Add opt-in control plane private endpoint authorization and deterministic subnet stitching to enable safe in-place upgrades and cross-account endpoint acceptance. Admins must opt into 'endpoint_authorization_enabled' and follow the new runbooks for cross-account flows.
notes_for_ops: Operations: enable feature behind feature flag; provision maintenance subnets with stitch:allow tags; follow docs/private-installer/subnet-stitching.md for a staged rollout. If rollback is required, use bin/rwpi subnet stitch --rollback-window <days> to revert within configured TTL.
